label: copy phase of very short (L=3) sequences
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase (t > L); it never fires on original-token steps or the <DEL> step. Its core is short sequences: for L=3 it fires on about 96% of copy steps (both remaining outputs, recall_idx 1 and 2), and this holds 67% of the activation mass, including essentially all of the top quartile. The strongest activations are at the final step of L=3 sequences, especially when the input is g, y or b. For L=4 it fires more weakly and depends on the token, mostly at the second-to-last copy step when the input is g, 0 or y (precision about 84% for that clause). The remaining mass (about 24%) is weak, scattered early-copy firing in longer sequences (L>=5), with a small bump at t=12 for L=9; no simple rule captures it. It does not fire for any phase-0 input or on first occurrences of a token.
